summary: This benchmark evaluates early cost-curve aggregation versus late estimate averaging for two-camera depth estimation on DTU dataset scans. The findings demonstrate that joint matching significantly improves depth recovery over individual views and avoids the severe degradation of late-stage averaging, supported by paired bootstrap statistics.
strengths: Rigorous experimental controls that isolate early evidence aggregation from hypothesis budget or patch size variations.
Strong empirical demonstration of why post-hoc averaging of depth estimates fails compared to early matching-cost fusion.
Thorough statistical validation using paired bootstrap confidence intervals (+8.72 to +11.90 pp on scan 1 and +4.72 to +7.57 pp on scan 6).
Balanced error accounting highlighting both net recoveries (784 points) and failure modes where joint matching underperformed individual views (676 and 874 points).
weaknesses: Limited empirical scope restricted to only two DTU tabletop scenes, leaving performance across diverse topologies and textures unexamined.
Modest conceptual novelty, as early cost-volume aggregation and multi-view correlation averaging are well-established foundational practices in multi-view stereopsis.
Lacks exploration of robust aggregation strategies (such as truncated costs or visibility masking) to prevent occluded views from corrupting the joint score.
suggestions: Expand evaluation across additional DTU scenes and outdoor benchmarks (e.g., Tanks and Temples) to verify generalizability under varied illumination and geometric complexity.
Incorporate and test robust cost fusion techniques (e.g., top-k scoring or occlusion-aware weighting) to mitigate cases where averaging corrupts a valid single-camera estimate.
Include an analysis of computational overhead and scaling behavior when extending the joint matching framework to three or more views.

claims.text: Projected structured-light point positions select common-visible benchmark points and supply the scoring depth.

For every reference pixel and 96 inverse-depth candidates spanning 200–900 mm, project a common 7×7 grayscale patch into each candidate photo. Bilinearly sample each patch and compute its zero-mean normalized cross-correlation with the reference patch.
A baseline that averaged the two cameras' separately selected depths scored well below joint matching despite seeing the same photos.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Large Scale Multi-view Stereopsis Evaluation
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Utilizes the DTU evaluation framework and structured-light ground truth to isolate the specific performance delta between early correlation fusion and late estimate averaging.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Pixelwise View Selection for Unstructured Multi-View Stereo
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Provides a controlled two-view micro-benchmark specifically quantifying the pixel-level trade-offs (recoveries vs. degradations) of naive score averaging without full pipeline filtering.
